Method of Attack: Cryptomining botnet infecting Windows and Linux enterprise servers with Monero (XMRig) miner and self-spreader malware payloads
Multi-component architecture with miner and worm modules initially, upgraded to single binary capable of mining and auto-spreading
Aggressively scans Internet for vulnerable systems using exploits targeting remote code injection/execution vulnerabilities
Targets cloud workloads via remote code injection/execution vulnerabilities in PHPUnit, Apache Solar, Confluence, Laravel, JBoss, Jira, Sonatype, Oracle WebLogic, Apache Struts
Kills competing cryptocurrency miners after hacking into server
Spreads over network via brute force attacks using SSH private keys collected from infected servers
Lateral movement via SSH keys, bash history files, ssh config files, known_hosts files
Attack Vector: Remote code injection/remote code execution vulnerabilities
Brute force attacks using SSH private keys
Indicators of Compromise: Exploited vulnerabilities: CVE-2019-10758 (Mongo Express RCE), CVE-2017-11610 (XML-RPC), CVE-2020-16846 (Saltstack RCE), CVE-2018-7600 (Drupal Ajax RCE), ThinkPHP RCE (no CVE), XXL-JOB Unauth RCE (no CVE)

Other exploited vulnerabilities: CVE-2021-3129 (Laravel), CVE-2020-14882 (Oracle Weblogic), CVE-2019-3396 (Atlassian Confluence Server), CVE-2019-0193 (Apache Solr), CVE-2017-9841 (PHPUnit), CVE-2017-12149 (Jboss Application Server), CVE-2019-7238 (Sonatype Nexus Repository Manager)
Brute force attacks on Jenkins and WordPress
Monero wallets with collected XMR amounts
